correctness.rationale: The three-coordinate norm is exactly the maximum of the four contiguous-partition quadratic forms. Rewriting it as Euclidean square plus twice a maximum of four quadratic corrections reduces the global parallelogram quotient to a finite matrix-norm estimate. All nonexceptional matrix differences have operator norm at most 1/sqrt(2); the sole exceptional form has spectrum {1,-1/2,-1/2} and is handled by an explicit two-case scalar inequality. The displayed pair attains the bound exactly. No numerical sampling is used as proof.
